title: eks-deployment-drift-detector-terraform-module
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Create a reusable Terraform module and supporting automation that detects and reports configuration drift between Terraform state and the live EKS control plane configuration for Redwood Private deployments. The module should surface actionable diagnostics, run preflight validations before upgrades, and optionally trigger safe remediation or a canary rollback flow when divergences are detected.
background: We have recurring incidents where customer private EKS control planes diverge from our declared Terraform configuration after emergency on-host fixes, manual console changes, or out-of-band operator actions. Current upgrade and upgrade-canary flows assume state is authoritative, which sometimes results in failed upgrades or degraded KMS/role bindings across cross-account setups. Existing tickets focus on improving preflight checks and upgrade guardrails, but there is no focused automation that continuously detects drift and provides safe remediation hints targeted at the control plane layer (cluster API, IAM roles, KMS keys, control-plane node policies).
proposed_solution: Build a lightweight 'drift-detector' Terraform-aware module that integrates with the control-plane provisioner pipeline. Key components: (1) a terraform-plan runner (read-only) executed in CI/ops that runs against the remote state and compares to live cluster via AWS/GCP API queries; (2) a diagnoser that normalizes drift into categorized classes (iam, kms, endpoint-public-access, tags, apiServerConfig); (3) a flagging/alerting webhook to the Console/Slack with suggested remediation steps and a confidence score; (4) optional remediation playbooks: either an automated terraform apply in a gated canary environment or an ops-runbook with one-click PR generation that fixes drifted resources while preserving cluster availability.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable module exists in infra/terraform/modules/eks-drift-detector that can be included by priv controlplane stacks
CI job 'controlplane:drift-check' runs terraform plan against remote state and performs live API comparison within 15 minutes for a typical cluster
Detector produces structured diagnostics (type, resource, expected, observed, remediation) and POSTs them to a configured webhook endpoint
A Console alert is created for any high-confidence IAM or KMS drift with a link to a one-click PR generator template
Canary remediation flow can apply a limited terraform plan to a canary controlplane without impacting prod clusters and has automatic rollback on signature mismatch
Documentation and runbook are published (Confluence link) and a security review has been completed
tasks: Design: define drift taxonomy and mapping to terraform resource types
Prototype: terraform-plan runner container + live-API comparator (PoC)
Module: implement inputs/outputs and optional remediation toggle
CI: add controlplane:drift-check job with state locking and rate limits
Alerting: webhook integration + small Console inbox renderer
Canary: build gated apply pipeline for isolated canary clusters
Doc: runbook, failure modes, escalation steps, security checklist
Testing: staged e2e tests against dev/private clusters and synthetic drift scenarios
Rollout: opt-in for <10 pilot customers, monitor for 2 weeks, iterate
comments: 2026-01-12 Maya Rodriguez: Created ticket after postmortem for CL-442 — manual KMS rotation caused failed upgrades for three customers. Goal: reduce manual fixes and improve preflight fidelity.

2026-01-20 Liam OConnor: Spiked a PoC that runs 'terraform plan -detailed-exitcode' in a container; found several resources that terraform treats as 'tainted' due to autoscaling-group tag drift. PoC repo: infra/pocs/eks-drift-checker.

2026-02-02 Security Review (initial): Requested that the detector never expose secret values in alerts and that remediation applies run under restricted cross-account roles with MFA guardrails (not service-role). Assigned to Ops for cross-account role hardening.

2026-02-18 Design Review: Agreed on taxonomy (iam,kms,network,apiServer,addons). Decided remediation should be opt-in per-customer and default to 'report-only'. Canaries must be separate AWS accounts to avoid blast radius.

2026-03-01 Engineering Update: Implemented diagnoser and webhook integration. CI runner can run against state but flaps when IAM API rate limits hit; adding exponential backoff and caching of GetRole calls.

2026-03-10 Ops Note: Need a stable remote state snapshot stage; current S3 state with Dynamo lock is fine but we must freeze modification during canary plan. Blocked until locking policy is documented.

2026-03-14 Liam OConnor: Merged module scaffolding and initial tests to feature/eks-drift-detector. Opening PR to infra main for review. Next: integrate Console alerting and create pilot customer checklist.
